title: H229: Speaker-Role Weighted FinBERT on Earnings Calls (Large Dataset)
rationale: arXiv:2604.13260 (April 2026) analyzes 6.5M sentences from 16.4K S&P 500 earnings calls (2015–2025) using FinBERT with speaker-role segmentation. Finds monthly long-short alpha of 2.03% and OOS Spearman IC of 0.142. H168 (our prior speaker-role attempt) was NOT CONFIRMED due to OOS transcript coverage of only 26.5% — root cause was dataset size, not signal quality. This paper uses a far larger dataset (16.4K calls vs. H168's 2,086). H229 would retest the speaker-role FinBERT signal with improved data sourcing: (1) use the MotleyFool/SeekingAlpha transcript sources referenced in the paper, or (2) target EDGAR 8-K exhibit 99.1 items which often embed transcript text. If OOS coverage can be raised above 60% on the 30-stock universe, the signal should be testable. H229 design: long stocks with above-median FinBERT CEO-sentiment score AND positive score for Q&A analyst probes (negative analyst probes = bullish overreaction signal per the paper). Confirm threshold: OOS WR > 65% AND MeanRet > 3%.

H229 — Speaker-Role Weighted FinBERT on Earnings Call Transcripts

H168 failed due to low transcript OOS coverage (26.5%). H229 addresses this

Signal construction:

  2. Analyst Q&A probe sentiment (negative probes = management under pressure)
  3. Signal = CEO_score - 0.5 × analyst_negative_score
  Long top-6 by composite score, monthly rebalance.

Universe: 30 large-cap (same as H163/H174)
IS: 2013-2020, OOS: 2021-2026
Confirm: OOS WR > 65% AND MeanRet > 3% (must beat H174: WR=81.8%, MR=6.9%)

  Option B: SEC EDGAR 8-K exhibit 99.1 text extraction (EdgarTools)
  Option C: Motley Fool/Seeking Alpha scraping (ToS check required)
"""
